biography: Neil O'Brien, a name whispered with both admiration and exasperation in the Caterham Academy paddocks, hails from a small village in the Cotswolds. His journey began not on the track, but in his grandfather's garage, tinkering with vintage motorbikes. One fateful summer, while spectating at a local hill climb, the roar of the engines ignited a passion he couldn't ignore. He convinced his reluctant parents to invest in a second-hand kart, and the rest, as they say, is history. His early karting career was marked by raw talent and a penchant for flamboyant overtakes, often at the expense of consistency. A defining moment came at the National Karting Championship in 2018, where despite starting last due to a mechanical failure, he clawed his way to second place, showcasing his undeniable skill. Now, at 26, O'Brien is a rising star in the Caterham Academy, known for his aggressive style and unwavering belief in his own abilities. While victories have been interspersed with costly mistakes, his potential is undeniable, and many believe he's on the verge of a major breakthrough.
drivingStyle: O'Brien's driving style is characterized by an aggressive, almost reckless, approach. He's known for late braking and daring overtakes, often pushing the limits of his car and the track. While this boldness can lead to spectacular results, it also makes him prone to errors. He seems to thrive under pressure, often performing best in challenging conditions or when faced with stiff competition. Tire management is an area where he struggles, often sacrificing long-term pace for short bursts of speed. He relies heavily on instinct and feel, making him unpredictable but undeniably exciting to watch.

rivalries.reason: A clash of egos and driving styles. Rossi, known for her calculated precision, clashes with O'Brien's aggressive approach, leading to several on-track incidents.
A battle for championship points. Chen represents consistency, the very thing O'Brien lacks. Their contrasting approaches make them natural rivals.
Jake Miller is a childhood friend turned rival. Both come from the same village and got into racing around the same time. Neil has always seen Miller as a benchmark.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks, regardless of the weather.
Listens to the same heavy metal track before every race to 'pump himself up'.
Has a habit of adjusting his gloves obsessively at the start line.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser."
careerHighlight: Winning the Caterham Academy race at Brands Hatch in 2022. He started from pole and held off intense pressure from Rossi and Chen to secure his first major victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the Silverstone race in 2021. A reckless overtake attempt ended his race and cost him valuable championship points.
